outcome: A tested, repeatable failover you can actually schedule and prove, not a binder that only gets opened once something has gone wrong.
overview: Disaster recovery runbooks in an insurer are usually documents rather than procedures: written once, updated rarely, and executed by whoever is available on the day. Veeam Recovery Orchestrator turns the runbook into an executable plan that can be run against an isolated environment on a schedule, producing a report that says what recovered, in what order, and how long it took. The value is entirely in the testing: an orchestrated plan that has never been executed is the same document with better formatting.

benefits.text: The recovery runbook becomes an executable plan rather than a document
benefits.limits: Executability covers what the plan includes; dependencies outside it — network, identity, third-party services — still need to be represented or the test proves less than it appears to

benefits.text: Recovery can be tested in an isolated environment without affecting production
benefits.limits: An isolated test does not exercise production network and identity dependencies, and the report should state which of these were simulated

benefits.text: Each test produces a report evidencing what recovered and in what time
benefits.limits: Backup success rate is not recoverability; only a tested restore against a stated objective evidences it, and the two are routinely substituted for one another

residency: Runs against the customer’s own protection estate; no data leaves the customer environment

notFor.situation: An estate whose protection platform is not yet delivering reliable copies
notFor.why: Orchestrating recovery from unreliable copies automates an unreliable outcome

notFor.situation: A small estate with a handful of systems and a short recovery list
notFor.why: Orchestration overhead exceeds the value of automating a short manual runbook

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Veeam implementation partner · Duration: 8–12 weeks to executable plans with a first completed test cycle
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed testing programme.
1) Review — existing runbooks, application dependencies and stated recovery objectives
2) Design — plan structure, dependency encoding, isolated environment and reporting
3) Build — plans encoded and validated against the protection estate
4) Test and hand over — first scheduled execution completed and reported, cadence handed over
deliverables: An executed test produces a report stating recovery order, time and simulated dependencies
Recovery times are compared against the stated objective per application
The plan enforces recovery order rather than documenting it
